Background:
- Multi-tenant contact center platform serving mid-market retailers and fintech support teams. Primary product is agent desktop + automation workflows (Zendesk + Genesys connectors).
- Current LLM stack: OpenAI ChatCompletions + in-house caching/queue. Trying to migrate away from public token volatility and single-vendor rate limits.
Why Redwood?
- Need predictable latency under spikes (product launch / Black Friday simulators) — current infra has 300-700ms tail latency spikes, sometimes >1.5s when batch flushes.
- Interest in Dedicated pools + automatic fallback routing to cheaper model variants during capacity pressure.
- Tool-calling: must call Zendesk update API, internal KB retrieval, and actions (tag, escalate) with strong idempotency and safe retry semantics.
- Ticket summarization across long threads (20+ messages): want KV/prefix caching to avoid re-sending entire thread. Also want deterministic summarization (same prompt + model variant yield consistent concise summary).
- Cost sensitivity: unit economics matter for high-volume tenants; want Redwood Optimize to suggest batching/quantization profiles.

- CTO (Mar 2 call): "We need near-zero tail latency at the 99.9th — agents can't wait during peak support windows."

- Validate KV/prefix caching for long ticket summarization to measure token savings and latency improvements.
